content.title: What if you were in Madina that day!
content.subtitle: The moment the door opened, your familiar world might have stopped…
content.body:
Imagine someone standing before you, and by sheltering him, your family, wealth, safety, even homeland could face danger. Yet after knowing all this, if you said, “Come, even if it costs our last drop of blood, we will protect you,” what would you call that feeling?

They Came from a City That Was Itself Wounded

Madina was not the peaceful, serene city it is today. The city was wounded by the long, bloody civil war between Aws and Khazraj. Every speck of dust carried generations of sighs and revenge.

At such a critical moment, in Makkah’s mountain passes, in the darkness of Aqabah, history was written. Some yearning hearts from Yathrib heard the truth from the blessed lips of the beloved Prophet ﷺ. In that darkness, they pledged to protect him as they would their own families and children, risking their own lives. That devotion changed their identity forever. Rising above tribal identity, they became close to the Lord of the heavens. History remembered them as the “Ansar.”

Open Doors, Endless Hearts

After the Hijrah, when the Muhajirs arrived in Madina one by one, they had only tears and exhaustion. They had left wealth, property, businesses, and loved ones, arriving empty-handed.

But Madina did not let them be strangers. The Ansar opened not only their homes but their hearts. Sa‘d ibn Rabi‘ (ra.) told his Muhajir brother Abdur Rahman ibn Awf (ra.), “Take half my wealth today. Among my two wives, tell me which you prefer, and I will divorce her so that after her ‘iddah you may marry her.” Madina witnessed an unimaginable sacrifice.

Imagine yourself in Sa‘d’s (ra.) place. How deep must his love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have been to divide his lifetime’s wealth in a moment!

The Ultimate Test of Blood and Love

Love’s depth cannot be measured in happiness; its weight appears in the hardest moments. At Hunayn, when battle scattered everyone around them, the Ansar’s thunderous “Labbaik” and steadfast courage created an unforgettable history of returning.

After the battle, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed a large share of the spoils, including camels and goats, among newly converted Muslims from Makkah. Some young Ansar felt hurt. Understanding this, the Prophet ﷺ called them and said, “O Ansar! When the whole world returns with herds of camels and goats, are you not pleased to return with the Messenger of Allah?”

That day, tears wet the beards of the Ansar. The Prophet ﷺ declared, “If the whole world goes one way and the Ansar choose another valley, I will walk in the valley of the Ansar.”

An Unknown Ache Deep Within the Heart

The Ansar’s sacrifices and devotion are not merely history; they stir our hearts. From a hidden corner of the heart, a yearning question rises—

What if I had stood on Madina’s dusty roads that day?

What if the beloved Prophet ﷺ had knocked on my door with weary steps?

Could I have surrendered my worldly abundance, security, and family to him in a moment?

Perhaps this thought awakens a strange pain. The eyes become wet, and with a sigh the heart says, “I wish! If only I had been in Madina that day, if only I had been among the companions of the Ansar!”

Sources:

  • Sahih al-Bukhari: Hadith 3781 (Mu’akhah)

  • Sahih al-Bukhari: Hadith 4330, 4332 (Hunayn and the virtue of the Ansar)

  • Sahih al-Bukhari: Hadith 3785 (Love for the Ansar)

  • Sirat Ibn Hisham and Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Hijrah and Madina’s social context)
